newsitem.title: USA: Dow ends at record high but off day's peak.
newsitem.headline: Dow ends at record high but off day's peak.

text.p: Blue chip stocks rode a wave of heavy volume to a record closing high on Friday, but ended off their peaks after tobacco shares fell on news of a proposed landmark settlement with state negotiators.

The Dow Jones industrial average finished up 19.45 points at 7,796.51, off its session high of 7,834. The close eclipsed the previous record of 7,782.04 set last Friday. For the week, the index rose 14.47 points.

But the rally was not broad-based, with losing issues outpacing gainers by a ratio of 1,479 to 1,101. About 652.7 million shares changed hands on the New York Stock Exchange in its third busiest day ever.
Traders said "triple witching" expirations of individual and index options and index futures skewed the day's results and bloated volume.
"A lot of it has to do with the options expiration," said Alice Hook, first vice president at McDonald & Co. "That's kind of creating a false tone."
Tobacco stocks, which rallied Thursday in anticipation of a liability settlement deal, turned lower after an agreement was reached shortly before the session's end.
The agreement would require cigarette companies to pay $368.5 billion over 25 years to compensate states and smokers and to fund programmes to help people quit smoking.

"It seems the industry was willing to give up a lot in order to get rid of the litigation," said Allan Kaplan, tobacco industry analyst at Merrill Lynch & Co. Inc. "This agreement seems like it should be able to make it through Congress."
Philip Morris Cos Inc., one of the 30 Dow stocks, dropped 2-1/8 to 45-3/8. RJR Nabisco Holdings Corp. lost 1-1/8 to 34-3/4. Lorillard Tobacco Co. parent Loews Corp. fell 3-1/4 103-3/8.

Market players said a drop in long-term interest rates helped support stocks. The 30-year Treasury bond rose 7/32, or $2.19 on a $1,000 bond, reducing its yield to 6.66 percent from Thursday's close of 6.68 percent. The price and yield move in opposite directions.
International investors lured by Wall Street's bull run were also fuelling the rally in large-capitalisation stocks, said Morton Cohen, chairman of Clarion Partners, a hedge fund.
"There's a good deal of foreign money that's coming into the U.S. equity market," Cohen said. "I think it's automatically being directed towards the large caps."

Shares in Ikon Office Solutions Inc. fell 9-1/4 to 22-3/4 on the New York Stock Exchange after the company warned its earnings for its fiscal third and fourth quarters would not meet analysts' expectations.

Cone Mills Corp., a maker of denim and home furnishing fabrics, said business conditions in the second half the year may not improve as it had expected. J.P. Morgan Securities downgraded the stock, which ended down 1-3/8 to 8.

International Business Machines Corp. rose 1/4 to 89-7/8. A SoundView Financial analyst said the computer maker is "solidly on track for the quarter" despite recent earnings warnings from other technology companies.
Quaker Oats Co. gained 1-7/8 to 44, boosted by a rating upgrade from Goldman Sachs.
Great Plains Software Inc.'s stock more than doubled in value in its first day of trading, rising 16-3/8 to 32-3/8.
The Nasdaq composite fell 0.04 to 1,447.10, up 24.07 on the week.

The Standard & Poor's composite index of 500 stocks edged up 0.71 of a point to a new high of 898.70, up 5.43 on the week. The American Stock Exchange index fell 5.03 to 623.27, down 6.83 from last Friday.
The NYSE Composite index of all listed common stocks rose 0.08 to 467.84, a record. For the week, it rose 2.67. The average price per share ended unchanged.
The Wilshire Associates Equity Index -- the market value of NYSE, American and Nasdaq issues -- was at a new high of 8,484.51, up 3.53 points, or 0.01 percent.
